gap_rows.title: Outbound-file contract: deliverFile manifest and return, notice-fact read of rwb-comms, JSON field names and problem body, event schema subject and compatibility level not fixed by any source
gap_rows.source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 17 and 41; TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Ownership Map tables (notice, interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog) and API (four P2 admin rows); legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 11, 12 and 13; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG sections 12.2 and 12.5; Template and Rules v1 §R9
gap_rows.section: §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §12.2 REST consumed, §12.3 Events published, §12.5 Workflows and activities, §13 Solution plan
gap_rows.description: One combined row for the shape-level points that no source fixes for this contract. (1) The manifest of deliverFile: Architecture v5 slides 11 and 16 fix a claim-check manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count and an activity named deliverFile(manifest), but not the interface ID, the business date, the case IDs, the idempotency key, the claim-check link or the requesting service. (2) The return element of deliverFile and the internal split between the activity and a local workflow. (3) The notice-fact read behind INT-14: the legacy story read the notice table in process, notice belongs to P6, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 no notice-fact read, so the operation exists in this contract with no path, query or field name in any source. (4) The JSON field names of the four admin responses and the detail texts of the problem body. (5) The schema-registry subject of rwb.integration.events.v1 and its compatibility level. (6) Whether job_catalog holds rows for JOB-10 and JOB-11. (7) The naming difference between Architecture v5 slide 16 (/interface-runs) and the TSD appendix and Ownership Map (/admin/outbound-items and /admin/outbox/deliveries), recorded as a conflict in GAP-0647 and applied here.
gap_rows.evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Manifest: fileId, batchId, sha256, record count' and slide 16 'TMP Act: deliverFile(manifest), receiveFile'; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 'REST POST /notices (request) · GET /cases/{id}/notices' and no notice read by ID; TSD P2 v3 T-A.2 gives the four operations with their query parameters and error codes but no body shape; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 gives the columns of interface_config, outbound_item, processed_event, idempotency_key, outbox_event, outbox_delivery and job_catalog; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 11 reads notice.sent_date (DF-LEG-019) and notice.person_key (DF-LEG-030) from the notice table in process; the sibling integration story states that the manifest and the claim-check handoff are 'Not specified in the source documents'.
gap_rows.area: Integration (P2) outbound files: contract shapes, consumed notice read and event registry
gap_rows.proposed: Fix the manifest, the return element and the three typed failures in RWB-P2-E1007-CON and re-confirm them with rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale and rwb-reporting. Fix the notice-fact read in the rwb-comms contract with the notice ID, the sent date, the person key and the document ID. Publish one RFC 9457 problem-details body for the four admin operations with the six status codes of the TSD appendix. Fix the JSON names of the four responses in the OpenAPI document. Fix the registry subject and the compatibility level with the platform event owner. Leave the job_catalog rows to the job catalog read. Take the TSD and Ownership Map admin paths and record slide 16's naming as superseded.

asm_rows.text: rwb-integration is the service of legacy key RWB-E1-007 in wave 1 under epic RWB-SVC-P2, with schema rwb_integration, REST base /api/recovery/integration/v1, topic rwb.integration.events.v1, event names rwb.integration.<Event>.v1, task queue rwb-integration in namespace rwb-recovery and Java package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration; it runs as its own ACE database login with grants on its own schema only (DP-02), replacing the legacy shared recovery_svc identity, and the login name follows the rwb_integration schema name of Architecture v5 slide 29.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story runs as the shared recovery_svc identity and names the package recovery.integration.adapter; the target naming comes from Architecture v5 slides 20, 29 and 41 and from the naming rule of Template and Rules v1 §R4, and no source names the per-service login.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 16, 20, 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02; legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 3, 10 and 13.
asm_rows.confirm: ACE team and DBA (schema and login provisioning, RWB-PLT-DB)
asm_rows.impact: No behaviour changes; the story builds and tests against the rwb-integration login and the service package once both are allocated.

asm_rows.text: Only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views (Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37 and 45; ADR-010; DP-05), so every ACE fact an outbound file needs - the addressee and contact by contact_key, the account by account_key and the batch completeness of the business date - is read as one REST call to the rwb-source-data contract with a 2 s timeout, and rwb_integration holds no grant on the recovery schema; the TSD P2 Integration v3 wording that P2 reads the views directly (T1.1, T5.2, T6.2) is superseded.
asm_rows.why: Two sources disagree: Architecture v5 is precedence 1 and TSD P2 Integration v3 is precedence 6, so R-PREC makes the architecture win and the loser a conflict row.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37, 41 and 45; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T5.2 and T6.2; ADR-010; Template and Rules v1 §R3.
asm_rows.applied_in: §1 Story, §2 Business rationale, §8 BR2 and BR3, §11 Data, §12.2 REST consumed
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect and the ACE team for the view grant
asm_rows.impact: rwb-integration needs no SELECT grant on the recovery schema and adds one contract hop to every ACE fact read, built against the rwb-source-data fake.

asm_rows.text: rwb-integration never reads debt_sale_account: the INT-25 tape rows, their account keys and the lot reference arrive in the deliverFile manifest that rwb-debtsale sends when a lot is awarded, and the account facts behind those keys are read through the rwb-source-data contract; no copy of a debt-sale row and no cross-schema foreign key exists in rwb_integration.
asm_rows.why: The Ownership Map gives debt_sale_account to S6 rwb-debtsale and the FSD P2 v3 A1.5 boundary says a service never reads another service's table; the legacy story read the table in process.
asm_rows.read: Ownership Map tables (debt_sale_account, owner S6); FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 19; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-11; legacy RWB-E1-007 AC1 and section 11.
asm_rows.applied_in: §1 Story, §7 AC1 note, §11 Data, §12.2 REST consumed
asm_rows.confirm: rwb-debtsale owner and the rwb-integration contract owner
asm_rows.impact: The tape is built from a request manifest instead of a table read; the manifest is one more element the rwb-debtsale and rwb-integration contracts must agree.

asm_rows.text: There is no data lake (DP-17; Architecture v5 slides 2, 8, 37 and 44): the reporting extract of legacy INT-19 and JOB-15 is delivered to rwb-reporting through deliverFile(manifest), the decision and outcome feed of legacy INT-20 and JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision, and every legacy statement that builds or sends a lake file is retired rather than restated, with no lake target, no lake copy and no lake delivery row anywhere in the target.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 removes the data-lake connection and DP-17 retires INT-19 and INT-20 as lake interfaces, while the legacy story and the FSD P2 v3 A1.5 still describe two lake files.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8, 37, 44 and 45; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 2, 5 and 12.
asm_rows.applied_in: §2 Business rationale, §8 BR12, §12.6 Schedules, §12.9 Call-type summary, §18 Traceability
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-reporting and rwb-decision owners
asm_rows.impact: Two legacy file interfaces become one delivery call and one Kafka ingest; no lake row, no lake file and no lake delivery state exist in any document of this key.

asm_rows.text: Job ownership follows DP-17 and Architecture v5 slide 44: JOB-11 is the platform outbox relay that runs every minute in every service, JOB-10 is a bank-Airflow file window whose file is built and sent by rwb-integration (the slide 44 owner cell reads rwb-comms + integration, read here as the request and execute split), and JOB-13 and JOB-15 are removed with the data lake; the two file windows are not Temporal Schedules of this service.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slide 44 names two owners for JOB-10 and retires the shared job table, while the legacy story assumes one Quartz scheduler with the item table; the split has to be stated once for the app, infrastructure and operations stories.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 31, 32 and 44; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 (JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13, JOB-15); legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3 and section 12.
asm_rows.applied_in: §12.6 Schedules, §13 Solution plan, and the operations story §12.6
asm_rows.confirm: Platform event and workflow owners, and the bank Airflow owner
asm_rows.impact: The release registers no Schedule and no Quartz job; the window is a bank scheduler call and the relay is a platform interval.

asm_rows.text: MSG-P1-001 uses the FSD P2 Integration v3 wording, '{product} is from {date}. Today's data is not yet complete.', in place of the legacy story wording '{product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived.'.
asm_rows.why: R-PREC ranks the FSD (7) above the story masters (9), and the FSD P2 Integration v3 change note records the rewording of the stale-data message.
asm_rows.read: FSD P2 Integration v3 change note (version 3, 'Stale-data message MSG-P1-001 reworded') and VR-P2-001-1; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 14.
asm_rows.impact: The stale-file message text changes under the realignment; no identifier, no trigger and no behaviour changes.

asm_rows.text: The provided admin operations use the names of the TSD P2 Integration v3 appendix T-A and the Ownership Map on the service base: GET /admin/outbound-items, POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend, GET /admin/outbox/deliveries and POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend; the Architecture v5 slide 16 names GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, and that naming is superseded.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slide 16 and the TSD appendix disagree on the operation names; the Ownership Map and the sibling integration story of this key both use the TSD names, and the WP fixes them for this key.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16; TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Ownership Map API rows (GET /admin/outbound-items, POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend, GET /admin/outbox/deliveries, POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend); RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect and the gateway-bff owner
asm_rows.impact: The edge and the client build against the TSD names; a later alignment of slide 16 would be a documentation change only.

asm_rows.text: The legacy alert names rwb.integration.outbound.held and rwb.integration.outbound.failed are not event names of the target, because the service's events are FileDelivered and FileFailed on rwb.integration.events.v1 (DP-14); the held-file alert is an alert rule over the held-item series and the failed-file alert is an alert rule over FileFailed and the EXCEPTION status, both owned by the operations story.
asm_rows.why: DP-14 fixes event names as rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1 and Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 43 give this service exactly two events, so a third and fourth event name cannot stand.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 43 and 45; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-14; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 15.
asm_rows.applied_in: §2 Business rationale, §15 Screens and states, and the operations story §13 alert mapping
asm_rows.confirm: Platform observability owner (RWB-PLT-OBS) and the DevOps team
asm_rows.impact: The two alerts are metric rules and not topics; the data steward still receives both alerts, and no legacy event name is published.

asm_rows.text: deliverFile is an activity on queue rwb-integration that accepts the request manifest, checks freshness, writes the outbound_item in PENDING under the idempotency key and starts OutboundFileWorkflow with workflow ID <interfaceId>:<businessDate>, returning the item reference and status, while the file-level retry ladder runs as workflow timers from interface_config; the manifest carries fileId, batchId, sha256, recordCount, interfaceId, businessDate, caseIds, idempotencyKey, the claim-check link and the requesting service.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slide 16 names deliverFile(manifest) as an activity and slide 11 fixes a manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, but no source fixes the full payload, the return element or the internal split between the activity and a workflow.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 16; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 12 (activity contracts on rwb-<svc>); RWB-ITG-E1007-ITG sections 12.5 and 12.6.
asm_rows.applied_in: §12.5 Workflows and activities, §12.1 and the contract story §12.5
asm_rows.confirm: rwb-integration contract owner and the requesting service owners (rwb-comms, rwb-payment, rwb-debtsale, rwb-reporting)
asm_rows.impact: The four requesting services build against one manifest and one event outcome; a later change to the payload is a versioned contract change.

asm_rows.text: The interface_config version IF-2026.11 holds the outbound rows for INT-14, INT-19, INT-20 and INT-25 with direction OUTBOUND, max attempts 3 and retry intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes loaded by RW-REFADM, and the load refuses a row with direction INBOUND; whether the job_catalog holds rows for JOB-10 and JOB-11 is not settled, so this key writes no job_catalog row and leaves the question to the job catalog read of the service baseline.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story states the configuration version and its four outbound rows and refuses an INBOUND row, while no source says whether the two jobs of this key are catalogued after DP-17 and the slide 44 split.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 3, 12 and 13; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (interface_config, job_catalog) and API-P2-009; Architecture v5 slide 44.
asm_rows.applied_in: §3 Preconditions, §12.7 Tables owned, §13 Configuration and reference data
asm_rows.confirm: Reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) and the platform administrator (RW-PLATADM)
asm_rows.impact: The attempts, the intervals, the folders and the roles stay data; if the catalog needs the two rows, it is a data load and not a code change.

asm_rows.text: The contract is versioned in the path as /v1, an additive change is allowed inside a version, a breaking change needs a new version, and the schema registry subject of rwb.integration.events.v1 is BACKWARD compatible; the subject name itself and the compatibility level are platform values fixed by the event platform.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slide 11 fixes /v1 in the path, AsyncAPI per topic and a BACKWARD-compatible registry, but no source names the subject of this topic or the compatibility level per subject.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 6, 9, 11 and 41; Event and Messaging Design v4; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-14.
asm_rows.applied_in: §8 BR13, §12.3 Events published, and the contract story §8 BR13
asm_rows.impact: A change to the two events is gated by the compatibility check; the app and the requesting services see no value of their own change.

asm_rows.text: The notice facts behind INT-14 are read through the rwb-comms contract as one operation carrying the notice ID, the sent date, the person key and the document ID, and its path, query and JSON field names are fixed in the rwb-comms contract because no source names them.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story built the WIN file from the notice table in process (DF-LEG-019, DF-LEG-030), the notice table is P6's in the Ownership Map, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P6 no notice-fact read, so the operation exists but its path is named by no source.
asm_rows.read: Ownership Map tables (notice, owner P6); Architecture v5 slides 14 and 17; TSD P2 Integration v3 T3.1 (DF-LEG-019, DF-LEG-030, DF-DOC-006); legacy RWB-E1-007 section 11.
asm_rows.applied_in: §12.2 REST consumed, §12.5 Workflows and activities, and the contract story §12.2
asm_rows.confirm: rwb-comms owner (RWB-P6-E1007-APP) and the P6 contract stories
asm_rows.impact: One more consumed path is fixed in the rwb-comms contract; the file build reads no notice table and holds no copy.

asm_rows.text: One error envelope is used by all four admin operations: an RFC 9457 problem-details body carrying the status, a code, the message identifier, the detail and the trace id, with the status codes 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 of the TSD P2 v3 appendix; the response JSON field names and the detail texts are fixed in this contract.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slide 11 fixes RFC 9457 and the TSD appendix fixes the status codes, but no source fixes the body of this service or the JSON names of its four responses.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11; TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.2 (API-P2-001 to API-P2-004); legacy RWB-E1-007 section 12 (endpoints).
asm_rows.applied_in: §12.1 REST provided, and the contract story §12.1 and §14
asm_rows.confirm: rwb-integration contract owner and the gateway-bff owner
asm_rows.impact: The edge and the app share one error body; a later refinement is an additive contract change.
